questions.question_text:
A couple wants to save $\$24\,000$ in $5\text{ years}$ for a trip by depositing an equal amount at the end of each year into an account paying $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Calculate the required annual deposit, correct to the nearest cent.

options.why: Divided $\$24\,000$ by $5$ years, ignoring compound interest earned.
Used beginning-of-year payments, dividing the full-precision ordinary payment by $1.06$.
Treated the target as the future value of one initial deposit and divided by $1.06^5$ instead of the payment-series factor.

questions.solution_text:
The payments form $a+a(1.06)+\cdots+a(1.06)^4$.
$24000=a\dfrac{1.06^5-1}{0.06}$.
$a=\dfrac{1440}{1.06^5-1}\approx\$4257.51$.
There are $5$ end-of-year payments; the factor is evaluated without intermediate rounding.

questions.question_text:
A business needs $\$100\,000$ in $4\text{ years}$ to purchase new servers.
Equal deposits are made at the end of each quarter into a fund earning $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly.
Find the quarterly deposit $a$, correct to the nearest cent.

options.why: Divided $\$100\,000$ into $16$ equal quarterly payments without accounting for interest.
Treated payments as beginning-of-quarter deposits, dividing the ordinary payment by $1.02$.
Used only $4$ payments while retaining the quarterly rate $0.02$, instead of using $16$ quarterly payments.

questions.solution_text:
$r=0.08/4=0.02$, $n=4\times4=16$.
The payments form $a+a(1.02)+\cdots+a(1.02)^{15}$.
$100000=a\dfrac{1.02^{16}-1}{0.02}$.
$a=\dfrac{2000}{1.02^{16}-1}$.
The answer is $\$5365.02$, with no intermediate rounding.

questions.question_text:
Zack deposits $\$350$ at the end of each month into an annuity earning $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
How many whole months will it take for the balance to first exceed $\$15\,000$?

options.why: Rounded down from approximately $38.93$ months, leaving the balance below $\$15\,000$.
Ignored interest and chose the first whole number greater than $15000/350$.

options.text: The smallest whole number greater than $\dfrac{\ln(1+15000(0.06)/350)}{\ln(1.06)}$ months.
options.why: Used $0.06$ as the monthly rate instead of dividing the annual rate by $12$.

questions.solution_text:
$r=0.06/12=0.005$.
The payments form $350+350(1.005)+\cdots+350(1.005)^{n-1}$.
$350\dfrac{1.005^n-1}{0.005}>15000$.
$n>\dfrac{\ln(1+75/350)}{\ln(1.005)}\approx38.93$.
The first qualifying number is $39\text{ months}$; $38$ months is insufficient. The logarithm uses the exact fraction.

questions.question_text:
Deposits of $\$1500$ are made at the end of each year into an investment account earning $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the number of whole years required to reach a target of $\$30\,000$.

options.why: Truncated approximately $12.94$ years to $12$, leaving the fund below $\$30\,000$.
Divided $\$30\,000$ by $\$1500$ without including compound interest.
Omitted the added $1$, solving $1.07^n\geq1.4$ instead of $1.07^n\geq2.4$ and rounding up.

questions.solution_text:
The payments form $1500+1500(1.07)+\cdots+1500(1.07)^{n-1}$.
$1500\dfrac{1.07^n-1}{0.07}\geq30000$.
$1.07^n\geq2.4$.
$n\geq\dfrac{\ln2.4}{\ln1.07}\approx12.94$.
The smallest qualifying number is $13\text{ years}$; $12$ years is insufficient.

questions.question_text:
Option X deposits $\$800$ at the end of each quarter for $6\text{ years}$ at $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly.
Option Y deposits $\$400$ at the end of each quarter for $12\text{ years}$ at $8\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly.
Both deposit $\$19\,200$ in total.
What is the difference in future values, correct to the nearest cent?

options.why: Assumed identical future values because total deposits are both $\$19\,200$.
Assumed beginning-of-quarter payments, multiplying the unrounded ordinary-annuity difference by $1.02$.
Used annual deposits of $\$3200$ for $6$ years and $\$1600$ for $12$ years at $8\%$ compounded annually.

questions.solution_text:
$r=0.08/4=0.02$, $n_X=24$, $n_Y=48$.
The payment series are $800+800(1.02)+\cdots+800(1.02)^{23}$ and $400+400(1.02)+\cdots+400(1.02)^{47}$.
$FV_X=800\dfrac{1.02^{24}-1}{0.02}\approx\$24\,337.49$.
$FV_Y=400\dfrac{1.02^{48}-1}{0.02}\approx\$31\,741.41$.
Subtracting the unrounded expressions gives a difference of $\$7403.92$. Equal contribution totals do not imply equal interest.

questions.question_text:
An investor deposits $\$600$ at the end of each month into an annuity for $10\text{ years}$.
How much additional money is accumulated if the interest rate is $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly instead of $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly? Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.

options.why: Applied simple interest to all contributions for the full term, using $72000(0.072-0.048)(10)$.
Assumed beginning-of-month deposits, multiplying each ordinary future value by its own monthly growth factor.
Replaced the monthly deposits with end-of-year deposits of $\$7200$ and used annual compounding.

questions.solution_text:
$n=10\times12=120$, with monthly rates $0.004$ and $0.006$.
For each rate, the payments form $600+600(1+r)+\cdots+600(1+r)^{119}$.
$FV_1=600\dfrac{1.004^{120}-1}{0.004}$.
$FV_2=600\dfrac{1.006^{120}-1}{0.006}$.
The additional balance is $\$12\,822.63$.
Both plans contribute $\$72\,000$; subtract the full-precision balances before rounding.

questions.question_text:
A municipality plans to accumulate $\$1\,200\,000$ in a sinking fund over $15\text{ years}$ to build a recreation centre.
Interest is $5.4\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
Calculate the monthly contribution $a$ required at the end of each month, correct to the nearest cent.

options.why: Divided the target by $180$ months without accounting for compound interest.
Assumed beginning-of-month payments, dividing the full-precision ordinary contribution by $1.0045$.
Used $15$ payments instead of $180$ while retaining the monthly rate $0.0045$.

questions.question_text:
A fund starts with $\$0$. Contributions of $\$450$ are made at the end of each month, and interest is $6.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.
How many whole months will it take for the fund to first exceed $\$100\,000$?

options.why: Rounded the logarithmic boundary down, although $145$ payments leave the balance below $\$100\,000$.
Ignored interest and chose the smallest whole number greater than $100000/450$.
Ignored interest and rounded $100000/450$ to two decimal places instead of finding a whole payment period.

questions.solution_text:
$r=0.066/12=0.0055$.
The payments form $450+450(1.0055)+\cdots+450(1.0055)^{n-1}$.
$450\dfrac{1.0055^n-1}{0.0055}>100000$.
$1.0055^n>1+550/450=20/9$.
$n>\dfrac{\ln(20/9)}{\ln(1.0055)}$.
This boundary lies strictly between $145$ and $146$, so the answer is $146\text{ months}$. The balance after $145$ payments is below the target and after $146$ payments is above it.
